scenario: What is cloud computing?

options.text: Computing services delivered over the internet
Servers bought and run in your own building
Files stored only on portable USB drives
Software installed only on one laptop

explanation: Cloud computing delivers compute, storage, networking and more over the internet, usually paying only for what you use.

scenario: Under the shared responsibility model, which is ALWAYS the customer's responsibility, no matter the service type?
explanation: Customers always own their information and data, devices, and accounts and identities. Microsoft always owns the physical datacenter, network and hosts.

scenario: A company runs virtual machines in Azure (IaaS). Who is responsible for patching the VM's operating system?

options.note: Microsoft manages the hardware, not the guest OS in IaaS.

explanation: In IaaS, the customer manages the OS, apps and data. In PaaS, Microsoft manages the OS. In SaaS, Microsoft manages almost everything.

scenario: Which cloud model uses only infrastructure owned and used by a single organization?
explanation: A private cloud can be on premises or hosted, but it's dedicated to one organization.

scenario: A company keeps sensitive databases in its own datacenter but runs its website in Azure, connected together. Which cloud model is this?

options.note: Part of it is on premises.
Part of it is in Azure.
Shared by a group of organizations.

explanation: Hybrid cloud combines public and private clouds so data and apps can move between them.

scenario: A startup wants no upfront hardware costs and to pay only for the resources it uses. Which model describes this?
explanation: Cloud uses operational expenditure (OpEx): no upfront costs, and you pay for what you consume.

scenario: Buying physical servers for an on-premises datacenter is an example of what type of spending?
explanation: CapEx is upfront spending on physical infrastructure. Cloud spending is usually OpEx.

scenario: What does "serverless" mean in cloud computing?

options.text: The provider manages servers; you just run code
The app runs with no servers anywhere
options.note: Servers still exist; you don't manage them.

options.text: You must buy and rack your own servers
Apps can only run on your own laptop

explanation: With serverless services like Azure Functions, you're billed for execution and don't manage infrastructure.

scenario: An online store automatically adds more servers during a holiday sale and removes them afterward. Which cloud benefit is this?
explanation: Elasticity means resources scale out and in automatically with demand.

scenario: What is the difference between vertical and horizontal scaling?

options.text: Vertical adds power to a VM; horizontal adds more VMs
Vertical adds more VMs; horizontal adds power
Both mean moving to another region

explanation: Scaling up (vertical) increases CPU or RAM; scaling out (horizontal) adds instances.

scenario: What does high availability in the cloud mean?

options.text: Services stay running with minimal downtime
Services run in one datacenter only

explanation: Azure services have SLAs that state guaranteed uptime, such as 99.9% or higher.

scenario: What is a service-level agreement (SLA) in Azure?

options.text: Microsoft's uptime commitment for a service
A contract that fixes the price of each VM
A list of features planned for next year
A security certificate for Azure websites

explanation: SLAs are usually expressed as a percentage of uptime, with service credits if Microsoft misses them.

scenario: A company wants to be able to forecast its cloud costs and performance. Which cloud benefit is this?
explanation: Cloud predictability covers both performance (autoscale, load balancing) and cost (forecasting tools).

scenario: Which cloud benefit lets a company apply templates and policies so all deployments meet company standards?
explanation: Cloud governance features help enforce standards and compliance across resources.

scenario: What does reliability mean in cloud computing?

options.text: Recovering from failures and continuing to work
Running workloads in just one region

explanation: Decentralized, multi-region designs help workloads stay reliable even during outages.

scenario: Which describes managing cloud resources through the portal, CLI, APIs or automation?

options.note: Also a benefit, but this describes how you manage it.

explanation: "Management of the cloud" (autoscale, monitoring, templates) and "management in the cloud" (portal, CLI, APIs) are both manageability benefits; here the question is about the tools you use.

scenario: Which cloud service type gives the customer the most control over the operating system?
explanation: IaaS is the most flexible and requires the most management by the customer.

scenario: A team wants to deploy a web app without managing servers or operating systems, but still write its own code. Which service type fits?

options.note: You can't deploy your own code.

explanation: Azure App Service is a PaaS example.

scenario: A company uses Microsoft 365 for email and documents. Which service type is this?

options.note: You don't build apps on it.
A deployment model, not a service type.

explanation: SaaS delivers complete applications; the customer manages users and data.

scenario: A company is moving existing servers to the cloud with as few changes as possible (lift and shift). Which service type fits best?

options.note: Replaces the app instead of moving it.

explanation: IaaS virtual machines are closest to on-premises servers.

scenario: Which is an advantage of the public cloud?

options.text: No upfront hardware purchase is required

options.note: Public cloud is multi-tenant by default.

explanation: Public cloud offers quick provisioning, pay-as-you-go pricing and no hardware maintenance.

scenario: What is a key benefit of a private cloud?

options.text: No upfront hardware costs at all
options.note: Private clouds usually need hardware investment.

explanation: Private clouds suit strict compliance needs but require more investment and maintenance.

scenario: Which pricing option gives the biggest discount for a VM that will run continuously for three years?

options.note: Can be evicted at any time.

explanation: Reservations commit to 1 or 3 years for a discount. Spot VMs are cheap but can be evicted.

scenario: A batch job can be interrupted and restarted at any time. Which VM pricing option is cheapest?
explanation: Spot VMs use spare capacity at deep discounts and can be evicted when Azure needs the capacity back.

scenario: A company has existing Windows Server licenses with Software Assurance. How can it save on Azure VMs?

options.text: Use a larger VM size with more memory

explanation: Azure Hybrid Benefit reuses eligible on-premises Windows Server and SQL Server licenses.

scenario: Which describes the benefit of geo-distribution in Azure?

options.text: Running apps close to users worldwide
Keeping all data in a single building
Removing the need for any backups

explanation: Global regions reduce latency and support disaster recovery.

scenario: Which is an example of a serverless Azure service?
explanation: Functions run code in response to events and bill per execution on the Consumption plan.

scenario: What does "agility" mean as a cloud benefit?

options.text: Running only in one fixed region

explanation: Cloud resources can be provisioned in minutes, letting teams experiment and respond quickly.

scenario: Which security responsibility moves to Microsoft when a company switches from IaaS to PaaS?
explanation: In PaaS, Microsoft manages the OS and runtime; the customer still manages identities, data and apps.

scenario: What is multicloud?

options.text: Using more than one cloud provider
Using several regions of one provider
Running several VMs on one physical host
Using both IaaS and PaaS services together

explanation: Azure Arc helps manage resources across multicloud and hybrid environments.

scenario: Which statement about the cloud pay-as-you-go model is true?

options.text: You pay for resources while you use them
You pay a fixed amount whatever you use
You must pay for three years upfront

explanation: Pay-as-you-go offers flexibility; reservations and savings plans trade commitment for discounts.

scenario: Which is a benefit of the cloud for security?

options.text: Providers apply patches and protections at scale
Customers never need to secure anything

explanation: Cloud providers offer built-in security tools and maintain physical and platform security.

scenario: Which Azure savings option applies a discount across many VM sizes and regions in exchange for a fixed hourly spend commitment?

options.note: Uses spare capacity; not a commitment.

explanation: Savings plans offer flexibility across compute services; reservations are tied to specific resources.

scenario: What is an Azure region?

options.text: A single rack of physical servers
A billing account for a company
A group of users in Entra ID

explanation: Regions contain one or more datacenters connected by a low-latency network.

scenario: What is an availability zone?

options.text: A separate datacenter group within a region
A pair of regions in one country
A virtual network in a subscription
A backup copy of a VM

explanation: Each zone has independent power, cooling and networking. Enabled regions have at least three zones.

scenario: A VM must stay available if one datacenter in a region fails. What should be used?

options.text: Use a larger VM size with more memory
Add a second managed disk to the VM
Use a static public IP address

explanation: Zone-redundant deployments survive the loss of a single zone.

scenario: What is a region pair?

options.text: Two regions in one geography, paired for recovery
Two availability zones inside one datacenter
Two subscriptions that share one tenant
Two VMs sharing one load balancer

explanation: Region pairs are usually 300+ miles apart; platform updates roll out to one region at a time and recovery is prioritized for one in a pair.

scenario: Which describes Azure sovereign regions?

options.text: Isolated Azure instances for government or legal needs
Regions with the lowest prices worldwide
Regions reserved for testing new services
Regions that have no availability zones

explanation: Examples include Azure Government (US) and Azure operated by 21Vianet (China).

scenario: What is a resource group?

options.text: A logical container for related resources
A physical rack of servers in a datacenter
A security group of Entra ID users

explanation: Resources belong to exactly one resource group; deleting a group deletes everything in it.

scenario: Which statement about resource groups is correct?

options.text: A resource can be in only one resource group at a time
Resource groups can be nested inside each other
A resource can belong to several groups
Deleting a group keeps its resources

explanation: Resources can be moved between resource groups, but each resource has only one group.

scenario: What is an Azure subscription used for?

options.text: An address range for a virtual network

explanation: Organizations often use separate subscriptions for departments or environments like dev and production.

scenario: Which order shows the Azure hierarchy from top to bottom?

options.text: Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups, resources
Resources, resource groups, subscriptions, management groups
Subscriptions, management groups, resources, resource groups
Resource groups, management groups, resources, subscriptions

explanation: Policies and access applied at a higher level are inherited by everything below.

scenario: A company with 20 subscriptions wants to apply one policy to all of them at once. What should it use?
explanation: Management groups organize subscriptions so governance can be applied once and inherited.

scenario: What is an Azure resource?

options.text: A manageable item, like a VM or database
An Azure region and its datacenters

explanation: Resources are created and managed through Azure Resource Manager.

scenario: Which compute option gives full control of the operating system?
explanation: VMs are IaaS: you choose the OS and manage it.

scenario: A company needs many identical VMs that scale automatically with demand. What should it use?
explanation: Scale Sets create and manage groups of identical, load-balanced VMs.

scenario: What do availability sets protect against?

options.text: The loss of an entire Azure region
Accidental deletion of a VM's data

explanation: Availability sets spread VMs across fault domains (separate racks) and update domains (staggered updates).

scenario: Employees need a Windows desktop and apps they can use from any device, hosted in Azure. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure Virtual Desktop provides virtualized desktops and apps, including multi-session Windows.

scenario: Which resources are needed for an Azure VM to be created?

options.text: A virtual network, disks and a NIC
A management group and an Azure Policy
An App Service plan and web app
A Log Analytics workspace and agent

explanation: VMs also typically use a public IP (optional) and a network security group.

scenario: What is a container?

options.text: A lightweight package of an app and its dependencies
A full virtual machine with its own OS kernel
A storage folder in Blob Storage

explanation: Containers start quickly and run consistently across environments.

scenario: Which service runs containers quickly without managing servers or orchestration?
explanation: ACI is the simplest way to run a container; AKS manages large, orchestrated container workloads.

scenario: A company needs to orchestrate hundreds of containers with automatic scaling and rolling updates. Which service fits?
explanation: AKS is a managed Kubernetes service.

scenario: Which service hosts web apps and APIs without managing VMs?
explanation: App Service is PaaS with built-in scaling, deployment slots and support for many languages.

scenario: Which compute option bills only when code runs in response to events?
explanation: Functions are serverless and scale automatically.

scenario: What is an Azure virtual network (VNet)?

options.text: A private network for Azure resources
A physical cable between offices and Azure
A directory of users and groups

explanation: VNets provide isolation, internet communication, on-premises connectivity and traffic filtering.

scenario: What is a subnet?

options.text: An IP address range within a VNet
A type of storage account for networks

explanation: Subnets segment a VNet so resources can be organized and secured.

scenario: Two virtual networks need to communicate privately over the Microsoft backbone. What should be used?

options.text: A public IP on each VM

explanation: Peering connects VNets in the same or different regions (global peering).

scenario: An office needs an encrypted connection over the internet to an Azure virtual network. What should be used?

options.note: Private connection, not over the internet.

explanation: VPN Gateway supports site-to-site, point-to-site and VNet-to-VNet connections.

scenario: A company needs a private connection to Azure that doesn't go over the public internet. Which service fits?
explanation: ExpressRoute provides a dedicated private connection through a connectivity provider.

scenario: Which Azure service hosts DNS domains and resolves names using Azure infrastructure?
explanation: Azure DNS lets you manage DNS records with the same credentials, billing and tools as other Azure services.

scenario: What is a private endpoint?

options.text: A private IP for a service, inside your VNet
A public URL for a storage account
A VPN client app for remote workers
A backup copy of a virtual network

explanation: Private endpoints (Azure Private Link) keep traffic to PaaS services on the private network.

scenario: By default, how can a storage account be reached?

options.text: Through a public endpoint, with authentication
Only from VMs in the same subnet
Only after a private endpoint is created

explanation: You can restrict public access and use private endpoints for private-only access.

scenario: Which Azure Storage service is best for unstructured data like images and videos?
explanation: Blob Storage stores massive amounts of unstructured object data.

scenario: A team needs a shared network file share that Windows and Linux machines can mount using SMB. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure Files supports SMB and NFS shares that can be mounted in the cloud or on premises.

scenario: Which storage service passes messages between application components?
explanation: Queues decouple components and buffer work.

scenario: Which storage access tier is cheapest for data that is rarely accessed and can wait hours to be retrieved?

options.note: For data kept 30+ days, accessed infrequently.
For data kept 90+ days with faster access than Archive.

explanation: Archive is offline storage; data must be rehydrated, which can take hours. Its minimum storage period is 180 days.

scenario: Data is accessed infrequently and kept for at least 30 days, but must be available immediately. Which tier fits best?

options.note: Higher storage cost for infrequent access.

explanation: Cool has lower storage cost and higher access cost than Hot.

scenario: Which redundancy option keeps three copies of data in a single datacenter?
explanation: LRS is the cheapest option and protects against drive and rack failures, not a datacenter disaster.

scenario: Data must survive the loss of an entire region. Which redundancy option fits?
explanation: GRS copies data to a secondary region. RA-GRS also allows reads from the secondary.

scenario: Which redundancy option copies data across three availability zones in one region?

options.note: Read access to a second region.

explanation: ZRS keeps data available if one zone fails.

scenario: Which tool copies large amounts of data to or from Azure Storage from the command line?
explanation: AzCopy is a command-line utility for copying blobs and files.

scenario: Which free graphical tool lets users browse and manage storage accounts on their desktop?
explanation: Storage Explorer uses AzCopy behind the scenes for transfers.

scenario: A company wants its on-premises Windows file servers to cache files from Azure Files. Which service fits?
explanation: File Sync turns Windows Servers into fast caches of Azure file shares.

scenario: A company must move 60 TB of data to Azure, but its internet connection is slow. What should it use?
explanation: Data Box is a physical device shipped to you, loaded with data, then shipped back to Azure.

scenario: Which service discovers on-premises servers and assesses and migrates them to Azure?
explanation: Azure Migrate is a central hub for discovery, assessment and migration.

scenario: What is Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: A database service for cloud apps
A file sharing service for teams

explanation: Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) handles sign-in, SSO, MFA and app access.

scenario: Legacy apps in Azure need domain join, Group Policy and Kerberos without running domain controllers. Which service fits?

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID with no add-ons
options.note: Doesn't provide traditional domain join or Kerberos for VMs.

explanation: Entra Domain Services provides managed domain services compatible with Active Directory.

scenario: Users sign in once and access many applications without signing in again. What is this?
explanation: SSO reduces passwords to remember and simplifies access management.

scenario: Which is an example of multifactor authentication (MFA)?

options.text: A password plus a phone app code
A password typed in twice to confirm
A very long, complex password only
A username and a strong password

explanation: MFA combines something you know, something you have and something you are.

scenario: Which authentication method lets users sign in without a password, such as with Windows Hello or a FIDO2 key?
explanation: Passwordless methods are more secure and convenient.

scenario: A company wants partner users to sign in to its apps with their own credentials. Which feature fits?
explanation: External identities let people outside the organization access resources using their own accounts.

scenario: A company wants MFA only when users sign in from outside the office network. Which feature fits?
explanation: Conditional Access uses signals like location, device and risk to decide access requirements.

scenario: A user should be able to view resources in a resource group but not change them. What should be assigned?

options.text: The Owner role on the group
The Contributor role on the group
A delete lock on the group

explanation: Azure role-based access control grants permissions at management group, subscription, resource group or resource scope.

scenario: What is the principle of Zero Trust?

options.text: Never trust, always verify every request
Trust everything inside the corporate network

explanation: Zero Trust: verify explicitly, use least privilege access and assume breach.

scenario: What is defense in depth?

options.text: Multiple layers of security protecting data
A single strong firewall at the edge

explanation: Layers include physical security, identity, perimeter, network, compute, application and data.

scenario: Which service assesses security posture and protects workloads across Azure, on-premises and other clouds?
explanation: Defender for Cloud provides a secure score, recommendations and threat protection.

scenario: Which factor can increase Azure costs?

options.note: Inbound data transfer is generally free.

explanation: Cost factors include resource type, consumption, region, bandwidth (egress) and reservations.

scenario: Why might the same VM cost more in one region than another?

options.text: Costs depend on the user's time zone

explanation: Location affects pricing because of local costs, taxes and demand.

scenario: A company wants to estimate the monthly cost of a new Azure solution before deploying it. Which tool should it use?
explanation: The pricing calculator estimates costs for specific services and configurations.

scenario: Which tool shows current spending, forecasts and budgets with alerts for an Azure subscription?
explanation: Cost Management analyzes costs, sets budgets and sends alerts when spending reaches thresholds.

scenario: Finance wants an email when a department's Azure spending reaches 80% of its monthly amount. What should be set up?

options.note: Policy controls resource settings, not spending alerts.
Tags help group costs but don't send alerts.

explanation: Budgets can alert at thresholds; they don't stop resources automatically by themselves.

scenario: What are tags used for in Azure?
explanation: Tags such as Department=Finance help with cost reporting, automation and organization.

scenario: Finance needs costs broken down by department across several resource groups. What should be applied to resources?
explanation: Cost Management can group and filter costs by tag.

scenario: A company must ensure resources are only created in approved regions. Which service enforces this?

options.note: Controls who can act, not what settings are allowed.

explanation: Azure Policy evaluates resources against rules and can deny noncompliant deployments.

scenario: What is the difference between Azure Policy and Azure RBAC?

options.text: Policy controls resource settings; RBAC controls user permissions
Policy controls user permissions; RBAC controls settings

explanation: RBAC decides who can do what; Policy decides what resources and configurations are allowed.

scenario: Which resource lock prevents a resource from being deleted but still allows changes?
explanation: Locks apply to everyone, including owners, until the lock is removed.

scenario: A production database must not be changed or deleted by anyone, even administrators, without first removing a safeguard. What should be applied?
explanation: ReadOnly locks block changes and deletion until removed.

scenario: Which service helps discover, classify and govern data across on-premises, multicloud and SaaS sources?
explanation: Purview provides data governance, data catalog, and risk and compliance solutions.

scenario: Which statement about Azure Policy is true?

options.text: It audits resources and can block noncompliant ones
It only works on virtual machines
It grants users permissions to resources
It can't be assigned to subscriptions

explanation: Policies can be grouped into initiatives and assigned at management group, subscription or resource group scope.

scenario: Where should a policy be assigned so it applies to every subscription in a company?
explanation: Assignments are inherited by child scopes.

scenario: Which tool provides a web-based graphical interface to manage Azure resources?
explanation: The portal lets you build, manage and monitor resources and create dashboards.

scenario: An admin wants a browser-based shell with Azure CLI and PowerShell ready to use, without installing anything. What should they use?
explanation: Cloud Shell runs in the browser and is authenticated with your Azure account.

scenario: Which command-line tools can manage Azure resources from Windows, macOS or Linux?
explanation: Azure CLI uses bash-style commands; Azure PowerShell uses cmdlets. Both are cross-platform.

scenario: What is Azure Resource Manager (ARM)?

options.text: A tool for copying files to storage
A type of virtual machine image

explanation: Every request from the portal, CLI, PowerShell or APIs goes through ARM.

scenario: A team wants to deploy the same set of resources consistently every time using a JSON file. What should it use?
explanation: ARM templates are declarative infrastructure as code. Bicep is a simpler language that compiles to ARM.

scenario: What is infrastructure as code (IaC)?

options.text: Writing application code inside a VM
Storing source code in Blob Storage

explanation: IaC makes deployments repeatable, reviewable and version controlled.

scenario: A company wants to manage its on-premises servers and other clouds' Kubernetes clusters from Azure. Which service fits?
explanation: Azure Arc extends Azure management, policy and monitoring to resources outside Azure.

scenario: What is a benefit of using ARM templates over manual portal deployments?
explanation: Templates can be deployed many times to create identical environments.

scenario: Which service gives personalized recommendations to improve cost, security, reliability and performance?
explanation: Advisor covers reliability, security, performance, cost and operational excellence.

scenario: A user wants to know whether an Azure outage is affecting their resources. Which service should they check?
explanation: Service Health shows Azure-wide status, service issues and planned maintenance for your services, and Resource Health for specific resources.

scenario: Which service collects and analyzes metrics and logs from Azure and on-premises resources?
explanation: Azure Monitor includes metrics, Log Analytics, alerts and Application Insights.

scenario: An admin wants to write queries over collected log data. Which tool should they use?
explanation: Log Analytics uses Kusto Query Language (KQL).

scenario: Developers want to monitor a web app's performance, failures and user behavior. Which feature fits?
explanation: Application Insights is part of Azure Monitor and provides application performance monitoring.

scenario: An admin wants to be notified when a VM's CPU stays above 90% for 10 minutes. What should be created?
explanation: Alerts can notify by email, SMS or trigger actions through action groups.

scenario: Which part of Service Health shows the health of an individual resource, like a specific VM?
explanation: Service Health includes Azure status, service health and Resource Health.

scenario: Which Azure tool would recommend resizing or shutting down underused VMs to save money?
explanation: Advisor's cost recommendations identify idle and underused resources.

scenario: What does a service level agreement credit mean for customers?

options.text: A refund when uptime targets are missed
A credit card used for Azure billing

explanation: If a service misses its SLA, customers can request service credits.

scenario: How does deploying a VM across availability zones affect its SLA?

options.text: It has no effect on the SLA

explanation: Multi-instance and multi-zone deployments qualify for higher SLAs than a single VM.

scenario: Which is a correct use of Azure resource tags?

options.text: Identifying the cost center or owner of a resource
Preventing a resource from being deleted

explanation: Tags don't affect security or behavior unless policies or automation use them.

scenario: Which describes a benefit of using management groups?

options.text: Reducing the price of every VM

explanation: Management groups can be nested to reflect an organization's structure.

scenario: A company wants Azure Policy to automatically add a missing tag to new resources. What can the policy do?

options.text: Modify the resource to add the tag

explanation: Policy effects include audit, deny, append, modify and deploy-if-not-exists.

scenario: Which statement about Azure Cost Management is true?

options.text: It can analyze costs by tag, resource group or service
It only works for one VM

explanation: Use cost analysis views and exports to understand spending.

scenario: What is the Azure Monitor agent used for?
explanation: The agent sends guest OS logs and performance data to Azure Monitor.

scenario: Which is an example of using infrastructure as code with Azure?

options.text: Deploying resources from a Bicep file
Clicking through the portal each time

explanation: Bicep files are compiled to ARM templates for deployment.

scenario: Who can remove a resource lock?

options.text: Users allowed to manage locks, like Owner
Anyone with Reader access to it
No one, because locks are permanent

explanation: Locks protect against accidents; authorized users must remove the lock before changing or deleting the resource.

scenario: A company wants to see whether its resources comply with regulatory standards and its own rules. Which service shows compliance state?
explanation: Policy shows which resources are compliant or noncompliant with assigned policies.

scenario: Which describes Azure Monitor alerts' action groups?

options.text: Who to notify and what to run on an alert
A list of resource groups to clean up
A set of VM sizes to scale between
A collection of storage access tiers

explanation: Action groups can send emails or SMS, or trigger automation like Logic Apps or functions.
